display_name: Vasse Felix Filius Cabernet, Margaret River
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "From Margaret River's gravelly loams and Forest Grove ironstone comes the Filius Cabernet, a Cabernet-dominant blend spiked with 4% Côt (Malbec) and 1% Petit Verdot that supplies violet lift and extra tannic grip. In market terms it sits as an everyday-value expression of Vasse Felix's estate Cabernet at a Spec's price around $26.",
  "wine_summary": "Vasse Felix matters in Margaret River because it was an early estate with sizable plantings on the region's western cape; Filius is their more accessible Cabernet blend that channels the region's maritime climate rather than reserve extraction. The blend leans on Cabernet Sauvignon's structure and cassis, Merlot for flesh, Côt for depth of color, and Petit Verdot for spice and tannin—each component tuned to wines grown on red gravelly loam, loamy gravel over clay and pockets of Forest Grove ironstone found in the appellation.",
  "terroir_expression": "Maritime-influenced Mediterranean climate—cooling Indian Ocean sea breezes and a long, dry ripening season—combined with red gravelly loam and loamy gravel over clay produces Cabernet with lifted black-fruit aromatics, linear acid, and firm but polished tannins; Forest Grove ironstone contributes a slightly metallic, mineral bite and structural tannin that shows as grip and a stony finish in the glass.",
  "vinification_summary": "The Filius blend is assembled from Cabernet-led lots with small percentages of Merlot, Côt and Petit Verdot; specific élevage details are not published for this bottling, but the vintage ABV spread (12.5% in 2023 versus 14–14.5% in older vintages) signals differences in ripeness and harvest timing—lower ABV implies earlier picking that preserves malic acidity, while higher ABV years reflect riper phenolics and fuller extraction. Petit Verdot's role here is technical as much as aromatic: even at 1% it raises tannin and violet spice.",
  "food_pairing": "1) Chargrilled lamb cutlets with rosemary and garlic — the wine's tannic grip and ironstone-derived mineral notes cut fat and echo the gamey lamb. 2) Slow-braised beef short ribs with a dark cherry and red-wine reduction — concentrated black-fruit notes and sturdy tannins stand up to braised richness. 3) Nashville hot chicken sandwich with pickles and slaw — the fruit lift and moderate acidity refresh the palate against spicy heat and fried fat. 4) Wild mushroom risotto finished with aged Parmesan (fine dining) — savory umami and earthy mushroom flavors harmonize with the wine's violet spice and firm structure. 5) Aged cheddar burger with caramelized onions (casual) — tannins trim the cheese fat while darker berry flavors mirror the caramelized onions.",
  "comparable_wines": "Moss Wood Cabernet Sauvignon — comparable for its Margaret River provenance and Cabernet focus, with similar marine-influenced acidity and structural tannins. Penfolds Koonunga Hill Cabernet Shiraz — comparable as a value-priced Australian Cabernet-led blend that trades reserve extraction for approachable fruit and broad retail availability.",
  "style_profile": "Medium- to full-bodied Cabernet blend with firm tannins and violet-spiced dark fruit",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink within the next 1–8 years for best balance; store at cellar temperatures (12–14°C) on its side away from light. Older vintages with higher ABV (2014/2017) will remain enjoyable toward the upper end of that range.",
  "value_assessment": "Price: $26–$27 (Spec's listings show $26.31). Competitors at this price band include Penfolds Koonunga Hill and Chateau Ste. Michelle Cabernet in many U.S. markets. This bottling is worth buying for drink-now Margaret River Cabernet character—black-fruit clarity, saline lift and tannic backbone—particularly for consumers who want estate provenance without cellar-worthy pricing.",
  "market_position": "Sold through mainstream retail (Spec's) and aimed at everyday-cabernet drinkers who want a taste of Margaret River terroir without premium cost; suitable for suburban bistros, wine bars with Australian lists, and consumers assembling approachable-case purchases rather than collectors. The bottle functions as a restaurant-by-the-glass pour where regional identity is desirable but price must stay moderate.",
  "insider_take": "Think of Filius as a pragmatic Margaret River Cab: it hands you the region's maritime freshness and ironstone grip rather than reserve tannin complexity. If you want a cellar candidate or a finely layered estate Cabernet, skip this and target Vasse Felix's flagship bottlings; if you want terroir-forward, affordable Cabernet for immediate drinking and food service, buy Filius.",
  "aging_potential_years": 8,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 1,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 8,

}

parsed.wine_summary: Vasse Felix matters in Margaret River because it was an early estate with sizable plantings on the region's western cape; Filius is their more accessible Cabernet blend that channels the region's maritime climate rather than reserve extraction. The blend leans on Cabernet Sauvignon's structure and cassis, Merlot for flesh, Côt for depth of color, and Petit Verdot for spice and tannin—each component tuned to wines grown on red gravelly loam, loamy gravel over clay and pockets of Forest Grove ironstone found in the appellation.

parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink within the next 1–8 years for best balance; store at cellar temperatures (12–14°C) on its side away from light. Older vintages with higher ABV (2014/2017) will remain enjoyable toward the upper end of that range.
parsed.value_assessment: Price: $26–$27 (Spec's listings show $26.31). Competitors at this price band include Penfolds Koonunga Hill and Chateau Ste. Michelle Cabernet in many U.S. markets. This bottling is worth buying for drink-now Margaret River Cabernet character—black-fruit clarity, saline lift and tannic backbone—particularly for consumers who want estate provenance without cellar-worthy pricing.
parsed.market_position: Sold through mainstream retail (Spec's) and aimed at everyday-cabernet drinkers who want a taste of Margaret River terroir without premium cost; suitable for suburban bistros, wine bars with Australian lists, and consumers assembling approachable-case purchases rather than collectors. The bottle functions as a restaurant-by-the-glass pour where regional identity is desirable but price must stay moderate.
parsed.insider_take: Think of Filius as a pragmatic Margaret River Cab: it hands you the region's maritime freshness and ironstone grip rather than reserve tannin complexity. If you want a cellar candidate or a finely layered estate Cabernet, skip this and target Vasse Felix's flagship bottlings; if you want terroir-forward, affordable Cabernet for immediate drinking and food service, buy Filius.
